question.worked_solution:
We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-1}{x}^{-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-2}]}_{a}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}]}_{a}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-1)^{2}}-\frac{1}{{a}^{2}}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
